locations_in_play._derivation: DERIVED 2026-09-20 under Ruling 8: assignments are populated and marked PROVISIONAL IN THE FIELD rather than left empty. The place roster and every place-to-type assignment live in grids/locations_registry.csv, which carries the two-layer structure of Ruling 1 - the geography system supplies TYPES, city bibles supply NAMES that map onto a type. Contested ground (Tremé, Marigny, French Quarter, Bywater, Red Lantern Faultline) is assigned there, not omitted. `match` distinguishes an exact place-name hit from an alias inference such as "the swamp" -> Honey Island Swamp. Ledger section 61.
locations_in_play._gap: PER-BOOK ROSTER IS NOT DERIVABLE AND IS NOT INVENTED HERE. No source maps places to books. The milestone grid names a location in only 3 of 9 books, so the entries below are the places this book's own milestones NAME - a floor, never a complete roster, and an empty list means no milestone in this book names a place, NOT that the book has no locations. Ruling 8 authorises deriving the TYPE layer, which is done; it does not supply a book dimension that no source contains. Listing the full 31-place roster under every book would assert that every place appears in every book, which is false. OPEN: a per-book location pass needs a source that does not yet exist. See CLAUDE.md section 4.

ruled_or_direction: The funder is an internal faction within Dominion, not a clean splinter that has left (supersedes "a Dominion splinter" in _concord_funder_thread_2026_10_18). Virelli's leadership wants resonance hidden and contained; the faction has concluded the secrecy will not hold (B02 is when it becomes unsustainable) and wants to own the public face of resonance when it breaks. It funds care, consent forms and goodwill and seeks firsts. The help is real; the motive is self-interest.
Virelli does not know at first; by B04, when he demands Lucien's return (M05), he suspects.
Partly sincere at the start; not a plain villain. "No redemption arc" applies to the faction's leadership, provisionally.
Baz believes he left Dominion but is still paid by it; he does not suspect in B01. The circle learning this around his death (end of B03) causes the split.

The protagonists' Concord is a loose collection of people trying to help, not a founded organization (refines "the organization is founded after the split"). The faction is the organization that later co-opts the name, when resonance goes public in Neon, and drifts into insincerity; the two collide. It collapses in Loom with Dominion's legacy.
"Dominion" is named once in B01, at C34 (approved).
Caldas: in B02 he pushes to escalate and is restrained by leadership; in B03 leadership gives him free rein (the lethal-pursuit rung). Direction ("Consider").
leaning: The split (and the loose collection coming to be Concord) leans to the B03→B04 boundary, tied to Baz's death; exact book not locked (author: "I lean 3 or 4").
possibility: Helena Kael is a possible member of the faction (not locked); her B02 request may be double-edged. Marius is not proposed.
provisional_funding_after_split: PROVISIONAL (10:02): after the split the loose network runs mainly on (a) open, public money Elisabet can sign for (a research grant or Nordic civil-protection funding tied to her crisis-data work), with written conditions and data owned by the people it is about, and (b) local mutual aid for the day-to-day, never one patron again. It gives Elisabet a reason to stay in New Orleans. Rex is not the funder; possibly a later infrastructure contributor in Neon or Loom. Option, not locked: if her grant comes with strings, she recognizes the pattern fastest.
